In light of some recent cries and claims I've heard since the One True Putt's latest announcement and coincident Voat update, I thought I'd investigate all of the users who have been banned from Voat since the change on February 12th.

If my counting is correct, 159 users were banned on February 12th (just taking the time to go through all of these I have to commend Putt on his time and effort with this, regardless of what the conclusion here is). Of these, only 10 accounts have not given any upvotes or downvotes whatsoever. A few of them have made comments or submissions, but most of these 10 had not even done that much. The other 149 accounts all have given out some upvotes, and of these 132 accounts only gave out upvotes, meaning 17 accounts both upvoted and downvoted comments or submissions.

Now, upvoting alone, given the right context, is enough to constitute vote manipulation. An account could be contributing to upvoting another account with does the dirty work in downvoting, or the aim could be to artificially upvote content in the first place. So I would say it is likely that 149 of these bannings are fully justified. Most of them were obvious alt accounts: in fact, with the exception of 14 accounts, all of the accounts banned on the 12th fit into one of four categories. These are: the cygnus_xxxxx accounts, the OAC_xxx accounts, the LORD_SPARTACUS_xxxxx accounts, or the JesusOfNazarethxx accounts.

The other fourteen accounts that were banned on the 12th are:

  • Trump4lyfe
  • sanegoatlswear (not the Sane we know and love)
  • pavelIwitz
  • 6AlBundy9
  • Phasemod
  • Saiga_Stonewear
  • StevenSonheimjew
  • nearbEar
  • kurwamac
  • Hqpflp77
  • Goathan
  • Goatku
  • mahalo
  • thunderIark (I think this guy managed the cygnus accounts)

Of the ten accounts that were banned without, at my checking, having any upvotes or downvotes given out, all of them fit into one of the four "obvious" farming accounts already mentioned. So it could easily be argued that they are guilty by association, for being "another of the same", and I think that's a fair argument. In the interest of avoiding controversy I think it might be best to wait until an account has actually been used towards the end of vote manipulation before banning it, but that said I understand after checking out all of these accounts how much time it must take to examine them, and if a view voteless accounts that fit into a party of vote manipulators, then I think that's justifiable. Putt obviously worked hard to get this much done.

To conclude, I would say our One True Putt has not abused any power or over-stepped any ground as yet in terms of the bannings. Note that all I've done is confirm the banned accounts actually did some voting, or otherwise matched up with other vote manipulators. I think that if one of the few cygnus accounts that has done no voting at all stepped forward and pleaded to be unbanned based on a lack of participation that it would be reasonable to unban that account, but at the first sign of vote manipulation a banning would then be fully justified.

I also don't know the stories of the 14 accounts I listed above, though I'm sure Putt understands exactly why they were banned. I believe all of these 14 had given out both upvotes and downvotes. Why or to whom, I do not know. If they wanted to appeal their bans, I think a "trial" would be just. But I suspect Putt knows what he's doing here.

I'll also mention that every single one of the 159 accounts banned since the 12th was banned because of "Vote Manipulation", at least that is the reason given for each in the ban log.

I will be making a post sometime later to discuss the state of Voat. For now, in terms of bannings, we seem to remain on the path of freedom.

Stay vigilant.
